references.text: Joshua had previously made a covenant with the Gibeonites and promised to let them live, which he now fulfills by protecting them.
The leaders of Israel had sworn an oath by the Lord, the God of Israel, that they would not kill the Gibeonites, and this oath was kept.
Joshua cursed the Gibeonites to be servants but spared their lives, as confirmed in this verse.
God's prohibition against shedding human blood establishes the principle of protecting human life, which Joshua follows here.
King Saul later broke this covenant by killing Gibeonites, showing the importance of the oath Joshua kept.
Rahab and her family were spared because of an oath, just as the Gibeonites were spared by Joshua.
